ai.description: *Cyrtodactylus srilekhae* reaches 55 mm SVL. It is brown with dark dorsal bands and a pale nuchal collar. Distinctive features include a slender body, granular scales, and lack of precloacal pores.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cyrtodactylus srilekhae* is best distinguished by its unique dorsal pattern of 4–5 broad, dark brown transverse bands that are distinctly edged with white or cream.
ai.habitat: *Cyrtodactylus srilekhae* inhabits the leaf litter and rocky crevices of moist deciduous and semi-evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically at mid-altitudes.
ai.behavior: *Cyrtodactylus srilekhae* is a strictly nocturnal gecko that spends its nights foraging for small invertebrates among leaf litter and rocky crevices on the forest floor.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cyrtodactylus srilekhae* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cyrtodactylus srilekhae* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in the Indian state of Kerala, typically found at mid-to-high elevations in montane forest habitats.
